judgments.topic: Characterization of the DTCC/Canton milestone arrangement
judgments.question: Is the coin earned under this arrangement noncash consideration for services rendered to the network, or a conditional nonmonetary grant/incentive?
judgments.proposedConclusion: Noncash consideration for services rendered to the network. DTCC earns coin by delivering participation and deliverables that benefit the Canton Network (a joint announcement, a production go-live, and driving settlement volume). This is an exchange of services for noncash consideration, best analogized to ASC 606-10-32-21 (measure noncash consideration at fair value), rather than a pure grant.
judgments.basis: The milestones are performance deliverables that provide value to the network counterparty (f_milestones); the arrangement is a bilateral agreement with the Canton Foundation (f_arrangement).

alternatives.conclusion: Conditional nonmonetary grant / incentive with performance conditions
alternatives.notes: Rejected as the primary model. Would recognize when conditions are met and receipt is probable. The economic substance here is closer to compensation for services benefiting the network than to a unilateral grant, but the recognition timing under either model converges on milestone approval.

judgments.topic: Measurement date and recognition timing for milestone coin
judgments.question: Is the coin's fair value measured once at contract inception (2026-01-15), or separately at each milestone's Accountability Committee approval / mint date?
judgments.proposedConclusion: Measure at each milestone's approval/mint date, not at inception. The coin is unminted and DTCC has no control until the Accountability Committee confirms the milestone and two-thirds of Super Validator operators mint it. The right to the coin is contingent on a governance approval outside DTCC's unilateral control, so the variable-consideration constraint (ASC 606-10-32-11) is not overcome, and no asset is obtained, until approval. Recognition and measurement therefore occur milestone-by-milestone on each approval/mint date.
judgments.basis: Coin is unminted until release and DTCC neither owns nor controls it at signing (f_unminted_until_release, f_no_control_at_inception); release requires committee confirmation and a two-thirds SV mint (f_committee_gate). This mirrors performance-condition logic (an award whose vesting depends on a condition outside the counterparty's control is measured/recognized when the condition is resolved).

alternatives.conclusion: Measure all 10,000,000 CC once at inception (2026-01-15) and treat milestones only as recognition-timing gates
alternatives.notes: Rejected. Although ASC 606-10-32-21 measures noncash consideration at inception when the entity has a right to it, here there is no right, asset, or control at inception because the coin is unminted and committee-gated. Fixing value at inception would recognize consideration DTCC cannot yet compel and would ignore the contingency. Retained as an alternative because an entity could elect an inception-measurement policy if it concluded the right was substantive at signing.

alternatives.conclusion: Do not recognize until all three milestones are complete
alternatives.notes: Rejected. Each milestone is separately verified, approved, and minted, so consideration is earned and measured milestone-by-milestone, not only in aggregate.
